scene_name: WeChat official account article topic ideas
scene_description: Topic ideation for opinion and commentary, how-to tutorials, industry analysis, personal stories and trending-topic explainers on a WeChat official account. Produces specific article topics that can be developed within the target length and match the account's positioning.

questions.question: What is the account's positioning or field?
What type of article do you want to write this time?
What style do you want for the article?
What is the account's update frequency?
What is the main goal of this article?
Which material or information must be included?
Which directions do you not want to write about?

skip_logic.description: Adjust the topics based on article type, style and goal.
rules: If the user picks "trending-topic explainer", ask about timeliness (within 24 hours / within 3 days); the topic must match the window, and add source verification to the risk warnings
If the style is "light and fun", switch to a playful tone; jokes are allowed but must stay decent and not weaken the argument
If the user picks "under 1,500 words", output single-argument topics only, not multi-topic roundups
If the goal is "product sales", ask about the product, and add advertising-law compliance and ad-labeling requirements to the risk warnings
If the user picks "daily", prefer sustainable, serializable directions and give series suggestions

tone_examples: Good: I watched this for three months; what is really worth saying is not the trending conclusion but one overlooked detail.
Good: Below, this method in three steps, each with an operation you can follow directly.
Bad: Shocking! You will regret it forever if you do not read this, 99% of people do not know!
Bad: Supposedly, some report said something, figure it out yourself.
conditional_notes: When the style is "light and fun", switch to a playful tone; colloquial language and jokes are fine, but facts and citations must stay accurate.
When the style is "emotional resonance", first-person narrative is allowed, but avoid fabricated experiences and over-sentimentalizing.
When the style is "deep and rigorous", switch to an academic tone, and key arguments must have sources.

constraint_list: The topic must be fully developable within the target length
The title must match the body; no clickbait
Opinions must be backed by facts, data or cases, and citations must be traceable
It must match the readers' expectations and the account's positioning
Information must be verified and accurate; trending explainers need reliable sources
Paragraph structure must suit phone reading, with a clear arc
exclusion_rules: Content unrelated to the account's positioning
Overly sensitive or controversial, baiting topics
Pure marketing posts with no substance (sales content must be labeled per rules)
Directions the user explicitly lists in excludes
